summary: All date/time parsing and building now lives in deskstats/timeparse.py with the exact public names from the guide; the other modules delegate to it and keep their public functions, and tests/test_timeparse.py is added. The existing tests pass, and original-vs-refactored comparisons (about 489,000 function results, 1,850 CLI runs across commands, options, formats and TZ settings) showed no differences. Two things in the guide disagree with the code, and I kept the code's behaviour: the section 3 table says chats use TRUNCATE, but chats.parse_ms rounds to the nearest even second (as section 2.3, sources.md and the changelog say), so chats use NEAREST_EVEN; and out-of-range inputs (epoch 'inf' or 1e30, year 10**20, 24:00 on 9999-12-31) still crash the CLI with exit 1 as before, but now raise a ValueError subclass that is also OverflowError/OSError.
